Collective delete-and-repair of mutually blocking clusters with massive random reinsertion and single-point soft-max Adam refinement followed by annealed global Adam and short wide-window LP jamming.
direction: Perform collective delete-and-repair surgery on clusters, since moving one rattler cannot change the bottleneck structure: choose a seed point appearing among the top 100 pairs, delete it together with 7, 11, or 19 points selected from its near neighbours with cosine above $0.30$ plus a few random points, then reinsert the deleted points sequentially, each time generating 30,000 random sphere candidates, scoring them against the current set, refining the best 20 with a single-point tangent Adam minimisation of the soft maximum at beta $500$ for 300 steps, and inserting the candidate with smallest true maximum cosine. After all reinsertions, run a short global Adam relaxation (beta $200\to1500$) followed by at most 3 seconds of wide-window LP, repeat with different cluster sizes and random seeds until 160 seconds, and accept the result only when its true maximum improves the incumbent, thereby forcing simultaneous relocation of mutually blocking points.

idea: Build a lattice-derived pool and greedy/SA discrete selection with antipodal-line variant, then anneal each topology with log-sum-exp Adam and LP jamming.
direction: Search independently for a structurally different, possibly symmetric or lattice-derived code rather than only perturbing the record: generate a large discrete candidate pool from normalized integer vectors supported on at most four coordinates with entries in $\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}$, together with all sign/permutation patterns of types $(1,1,0^7)/\sqrt2$, $(1,1,1,1,0^5)/2$, and $(3,1^8)/\sqrt{17}$; greedily select 182 candidates to minimise the evolving maximum cosine, improve the selection by simulated-annealing swaps of one selected vector against one pool vector, and in a parallel variant enforce antipodal symmetry by optimising 91 lines under $\max |\langle u_i,u_j\rangle|$ before releasing the symmetry. Continuously relax every promising discrete selection with annealed log-sum-exp Adam and the wide-window LP under a strict 160-second cap, and return the best among the relaxed discrete, antipodal-released, and loaded incumbent configurations if no new topology wins.
